## Introduction


## BLAST among contigs

```{bash}
if [ ! -e assembly.ndb ]; then
   makeblastdb -dbtype nucl \
               -in ../2023-05-15/assembly.fasta \
               -out assembly
fi

if [ ! -e selfblast.txt ]; then
   blastn -db assembly \
          -query ../2023-05-15/assembly.fasta \
          -out selfblast.txt \
          -outfmt "6 qacc sacc pident length qlen slen gaps evalue bitscore" \
          -evalue 1.0e-10 \
          -num_threads 24 \
          -max_hsps 1 \
          -max_target_seqs 2 1>blastn.out 2> blastn.err
   gawk '((/^contig/) && ($1 != $2)){
      print $0
   }' selfblast.txt > z1
   mv z1 selfblast.txt
fi
```

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(Biostrings)
assembly <- readDNAStringSet('../2023-05-15/assembly.fasta')
info <- read.table(
   '../2023-05-12/flye/ONT_PB/assembly_info.txt',
   col.names = c('ctg', 'len', 'cov', 'circ', 'rep', 'mult', 'alt', 'graph'))
info <- info[match(names(assembly), info$ctg), 1:6]
selfblast <- read.table(
   'selfblast.txt',
   col.names = c('qacc', 'sacc', 'pident', 'length', 'qlen',
                 'slen', 'gaps', 'evalue', 'bitscore'))
info$besthit <- selfblast[match(info$ctg, selfblast$qacc), 'sacc']
info$reciprocal <- info[match(info$besthit, info$ctg), 'besthit']
info$is.rbh <- info$ctg == info$reciprocal
info[is.na(info$is.rbh), 'is.rbh'] <- FALSE
```

Only `r sum(is.na(info$besthit))` contigs do not retrieve any BLAST
hit among the other contigs. They all are shorter than average.
Among the other `r sum(! is.na(info$besthit))` contigs, which do
find similarity in others, only a subset of `r length(unique(info$besthit))`
are themselves the best *hits* for other contigs. That is, there is
a small fraction of *reciprocal best hits*. Precisely, there are
only `r sum(info$ctg == info$reciprocal, na.rm = TRUE) / 2` pairs
of reciprocal best hits. Most contigs are not the
best hit of their own best hit. And it is a fraction of all contigs
which accumulate most of the hits. The difference in length could
explain this pattern: if a long contig holds homology to three other
contigs, it may be the best hit of all them, while only one of those
can be its own best hit. Not worth checking.

### Self-alignable fraction of the genome
Taken together, all best hits (reciprocal or not), what fraction of
the assembly do they represent? Ignoring the small contribution of
gaps to the length of the alignments, alignment lengths add up to
`r sum(selfblast$length)` bases. Taking into account that every
alignment takes two sequences, the fraction of the genome that is
included among best hits is half that number, namely
`r sprintf("%i", sum(selfblast$length) / 2)`, which represents
`r round(100 * (sum(selfblast$length) / 2) / sum(info$len), 2)`%
of the genome.

This is small enough to forget about it. Most of the assembly is
quite unique.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
RBH <- info[info$is.rbh, 'ctg']
selfblast$is.rbh <- selfblast$qacc %in% RBH
selfblast <- selfblast[order(selfblast$is.rbh),]
ggplot(data = selfblast,
       mapping = aes(x = length, y = pident, color = is.rbh)) +
   geom_point() + scale_x_continuous(trans = 'log')
```

### Contigs where reads did not map

```{bash}
if [ ! -e used.txt ]; then
   grep -v '^#' ../2023-05-18/crepi.vcf | \
   cut -f 1 | uniq > used.txt
fi
```

```{r}
used <- scan('used.txt', what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)
info$used <- info$ctg %in% used
info$uniq <- is.na(info$besthit)
table(info[, c('used', 'uniq')])
```

Among the `r length(assembly)` contigs in the assembly, most of
them get ddRAD reads mapped to them: `r length(used)`. The
`r sum(! info$used)` which did not constitute only the
`r round(sum(info[! info$used, 'len']) / sum(info$len) * 100, 2)`%
of the assembly's length. Quite irrelevant.
